data.reasoning: The only valid report (qwen3-235b-a22b-2507) thoroughly reviewed all 3 maintainer files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, post.install) and found no malicious behavior. The package is a standard VCS-based AUR package that clones the official upstream GitHub repository and uses a post-install script solely to echo user instructions. The second report resulted in a tool error (LLMResponseError) and carries no verdict signal.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the deepseek-v4-flash report, which failed to generate an LLM response for the PKGBUILD and consequently aborted the audit. This is not a genuine security disagreement but a missing verdict due to an API/model failure.
coverage_issues: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash failed with LLMResponseError, resulting in no files being successfully reviewed and no verdict provided.
learnings: Tool errors such as LLMResponseError should be caught and retried automatically before escalating to an adjudication workflow, as they create artificial disagreements and coverage gaps.
When an audit report ends in a tool error, the orchestration layer should treat it as a missing report rather than a conflicting verdict to avoid unnecessary judge overhead.
